subject: Clarify: retention of intermediate KV / streaming tokens and immediate purge options
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightbank.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightBank Security <sec-requests@brightbank.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: what exactly gets persisted from streaming sessions/KV cache?

Hi Dylan,

Quick question from our security reviewers while we finish the integration checklist: during a streaming generation or an interactive session, does Redwood ever persist intermediate artifacts to durable storage? Specific items they're asking about:

- partial/streamed tokens (i.e., intermediate chunks sent before finalization)
- KV cache snapshots (intermediate model state or minibatch caches)
- temporary prompt fragments or client-side concatenations before the final request

We need: a plain-language description of what is kept by default, any TTLs, and whether customers can request immediate purge of those intermediate artifacts (and what the purge path looks like). Also curious if the behavior differs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

If you can respond with an email we can attach to the SOC/Procurement review it would be helpful. We may follow up with specific data subject erasure requests.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
BrightBank - Platform Integrations

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, BrightBank Security <sec-requests@brightbank.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: what exactly gets persisted from streaming sessions/KV cache?

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR answers inline, followed by suggested ask items you can drop into the SOC pack.

1) Partial / streamed tokens:
- Default behavior (Hosted): streaming chunks are transmitted to your client as they are generated. By default we do NOT write streamed tokens to durable logs. Streams are assembled on the worker and forwarded; only the final request/response pair is eligible to be captured in logs if customer logging is enabled. In short: intermediate chunks are ephemeral at the worker level and are not stored to long-term storage by default.

2) KV cache snapshots / intermediate model state:
- Default behavior (Hosted & Dedicated): KV caches are kept in-memory on the serving process for the lifetime of the session to support fast stepwise generations. They are NOT serialized to persistent object storage under normal operation. We do produce ephemeral worker-level diagnostics (e.g., for debugging or postmortem) only when explicitly enabled by the customer or when a crash report is generated; those diagnostics are captured into an internal debug store with restricted access and a short retention.

3) Temporary prompt fragments / client-side concatenations:
- Clarify: prompts are treated as the request payload. Anything sent as part of the request is considered a request artifact. By default we capture requests and final outputs according to tenant logging settings (see capture controls below). If a customer sets capture=false or uses the "no_store" beta parameter, prompts and outputs are not persisted in our default capture pipeline.

Default retention numbers (Hosted):
- Captured requests & final outputs: 45 days retention by default (configurable for enterprise customers).
- Debug diagnostics (when enabled): 7–30 days depending on diagnostic level.
- Streaming/intermediate artifacts: not persisted; therefore no TTL.

Behavior differences by deployment:
- Hosted (default): as above; customers can opt-out of capture per-request or at the tenant level via account settings.
- Dedicated: admins can configure retention windows shorter or longer than hosted defaults. Managed-svc contracts typically allow custom TTLs and automated purge tooling.
- Private/on-prem: retention is customer-controlled — Redwood's control plane can be configured to not receive any request/response artifacts; physical storage and purge policies are under the customer's operational control.

Immediate purge / erasure process:
- Self-service: For Hosted customers with admin privileges we provide a console action to purge captured logs for a tenant or a specific session id. That action fires a backend job that erases objects from hot and cold storage and returns a purge-job id.
- Manual support route: If you need an organization-wide immediate purge and you cannot access the console, open a support ticket marked "expedited erasure" (we include the related_links below). We will run the purge pipeline and provide a job id + verification checksum.

Notes and caveats:
- If a customer has integrated our optional session-recording / audit-log addon, intermediate artifacts can be recorded by that addon (explicit opt-in). Those recordings follow the addon TTL and must be requested separately for deletion.
- Attachments to requests (files sent via file upload) are treated as customer files and follow the file retention policy; we keep file metadata even if the file contents are purged.

I'll attach a short SOC-friendly summary and an example payload showing the capture=false flag. If you'd like, Kimberly can jump in with wording for the compliance pack.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_retention_summary.pdf, example_payload_and_headers.txt

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightbank.com>

Cc: BrightBank Security <sec-requests@brightbank.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: what exactly gets persisted from streaming sessions/KV cache?

Thanks Dylan — very helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from the InfoSec reviewers:

- For the "ephemeral only on worker" statement re KV caches: can you provide a one-line statement we can include that says whether any worker-side snapshot is ever written to disk under normal operation? (They want a clear yes/no + short justification.)
- For the purge flow: will the purge job remove objects from backups and cold storage? We need confirmation that a supplied purge job id corresponds to a full erase (not just hot-store deletion).
- Finally, can you confirm whether Dedicated tenants get an SLA-backed purge timeline (for example, appears as completed within X hours)? If so, what is X?

If you can drop those three bullet answers into an email we can include them verbatim in the evidence pack.

Samir

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, BrightBank Security <sec-requests@brightbank.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: what exactly gets persisted from streaming sessions/KV cache?

Samir — answers below; feel free to paste these into your pack.

1) "Are KV caches written to disk under normal operation?"
Answer: No. Under normal, healthy operation KV caches are maintained in-memory on the serving process and are not serialized to persistent disk. The only time a worker-level cache is materialized to disk is in a controlled diagnostic/crash-report path (explicitly gated, access-restricted) or if a customer enables explicit debug capture.

2) "Does the purge job remove items from backups and cold storage?"
Answer: Yes. The standard purge pipeline removes objects from primary stores and initiates deletion requests for cold-archive tiers. For Hosted customers, the purge job attempts to remove copies from all Redwood-managed storage tiers and returns a purge-job id and completion report. Note: some third-party archival replication windows may impose short propagation delays; the completion report will indicate any pending replication artifacts.

3) "Dedicated tenant SLA for purge completion (is there an X hours)?"
Answer: For Dedicated tenants with an SLA clause we commit to an expedited purge timeline: typical completion within 24 hours for tenant-scoped erasure requests (subject to legal/forensic holds). Exact timelines are contract-dependent; we recommend adding a purge SLA addendum for any customer needing stricter guarantees.

If you want written evidence on Redwood letterhead we can produce a short statement for procurement (I will coordinate with Kimberly and Legal).

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Account Engineer, Redwood Inference
